survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results (means, proficiency-level shares, and subgroup gaps) using the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables rather than an author-estimated microdata model. The note does not specify whether student sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the production of the reported estimates, so the weighting approach is not directly auditable from the factsheet text. For analysts working with PISA microdata, complex survey weights are typically required to obtain population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds and to account for the multistage sampling of students within schools. When reproducing these figures, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and the corresponding variance estimation method recommended by the PISA technical documentation for the relevant tables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet is a descriptive reporting document that summarizes PISA 2022 results (trend lines, mean performance, and proficiency-level distributions) using OECD-published database tables, rather than presenting an original student-level predictive model with an explicit plausible-values (PV) workflow. Because the dependent outcomes are reported as proficiency levels and mean estimates already produced by OECD scaling procedures, the paper does not document PV combination rules or missing-data handling at the analysis stage. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported in the text provided, and the appropriate strategy is to follow the OECD PISA technical documentation for the underlying database tables.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is the set of students in Slovenia who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science: 6,721 students in 345 schools. The factsheet states this represents about 18,900 15-year-olds (an estimated 100% of the total population of 15-year-olds) and that all data met PISA quality standards for reporting. No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds or subgroup-specific exclusions) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet for Slovenia summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2 and Level 5/6), and subgroup gaps by socioeconomic status (ESCS), gender, and immigrant background, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. The assessment used two two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different item combinations, plus student and school questionnaires. Slovenia’s data met PISA quality standards, and the factsheet notes that an asterisk in other countries indicates sampling standards were not reached. The document is descriptive and comparative, so it does not estimate an original ML model or provide predictive performance metrics.
